title: Lemon and elderflower layer cake
subtitle: spring celebration layer cake with elderflower buttercream
excerpt: A lemon and elderflower layer cake pairs a sharp lemon sponge with a floral elderflower buttercream and a lemon curd filling. It's the kind of cake that tastes exactly as it should in late spring or early summer, bright, fragrant, and not too sweet. The elderflower cordial goes into the buttercream and the soaking syrup; the lemon curd goes between the layers.
sourceNotes: The combination of lemon and elderflower became a dominant British flavour pairing in baking from the 2010s onward, popularised in part by its use as the official flavour of the 2018 Royal Wedding cake made by Claire Ptak. Elderflower cordial has been made domestically in Britain for centuries, but its mainstream adoption in baking is relatively recent. The layer cake format here is the standard contemporary celebration version: multiple sponge layers with a separately flavoured filling and frosting, assembled in the American style rather than the traditional British sandwich cake format.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the unfrosted layers, well wrapped. Defrost at room temperature for 2 hours before assembling.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the sponge layers a day ahead. Make the lemon curd up to 1 week ahead.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 180°C or fan 160°C; skewer comes out clean when done

content.text: A lemon and elderflower layer cake gives you sharp lemon sponge, tart lemon curd between the layers, and a floral elderflower buttercream that ties the flavours together. The elderflower cordial does the heavy lifting in the frosting, use a good one. The lemon zest in the sponge is more important than the juice; don't skip it.

Preheat the oven to 180°C conventional (160°C fan). Grease and line three 20 cm round tins. Cream the butter and sugar until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time, mixing well after each. Add the lemon zest. Fold in the flour and baking powder alternately with the milk in three additions. Divide evenly among the tins and bake for 25 to 28 minutes until risen and a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tins for 10 minutes, then turn out.

Beat the softened butter for 2 minutes until very pale. Add the sifted icing sugar in two additions, beating well after each. Add the elderflower cordial and beat for a further 2 minutes until light and fluffy. Taste and adjust the elderflower level if needed, cordials vary in intensity.

Place the first sponge layer on a board. Spread with half the lemon curd, staying 1 cm from the edge, it will spread to the edge under the weight of the next layer. Pipe or spread a ring of buttercream around the edge to dam the curd. Add the second layer, repeat with the remaining curd and another buttercream dam, then add the third layer. Apply a crumb coat of buttercream all over and refrigerate for 20 minutes. Apply the final coat, smoothing with a palette knife. Serve at room temperature.
